top_signals.title: Apollo’s Slok Sees Iran War, Tariffs Driving US Yields Higher
top_signals.summary: Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, sees the US fiscal situation having little to do with upward pressure US yields. He says, “There are actually fewer worries about US policy making than there is in Japan and Germany.” (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Senegal To Rework Debt as It Reaches New IMF Deal
top_signals.summary: Senegal's eurobonds fell after the government said it will move forward with a "debt treatment" under the Group of 20's Common Framework. This came as Senegal agreed a new $2.2 billion program with the International Monetary Fund. Bloomberg's Chief Africa Correspondent Jennifer Zabasajja reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
